contribution.position: I hold my earlier position, with one correction to my own framing. I am answering qa (axis:risk), who says peak_memory is 380MB and comfortably inside the 512MB budget, citing artifact:perf-report. That figure does not appear in the artifact. The perf report records 740MB at peak load against the 512MB budget, which is about 45% over. Either qa is quoting a different run or a different report that is not in the artifact list, or the number is wrong. Until qa names the source of 380MB, the only measured value on record is 740MB, and the 'risk is contained' claim rests on a datum I cannot verify. The correction: the incident log says both sev2 incidents were retry storms, but it does not say they were memory-related. My link from memory overage to OOM kills to retry amplification is therefore an inference, not a documented cause. Nothing in the artifacts shows whether 512MB is a hard container limit or only a planning budget, or whether the worker has retry backoff or caps. Those two unknowns decide whether the overage matters. ops (axis:operability) cites runbook v4 for deploy and rollback steps, but the artifact says nothing about retry limits or memory-limit behavior. The runbook addresses recovery time, not whether the incident occurs. product's cost point (3% against a 5% ceiling) is not in dispute on its own axis. It does not cover the cost of any extra memory headroom if the budget is raised. Evidence that would change my view: a load test at the production memory limit showing no OOM kills, confirmation of retry backoff and caps, or a revised and approved memory budget with the 740MB figure reconciled.
